page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-4GB is a starter-tier virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 2 vCPUs and 2 physical cores at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 30 GB local SSD storage volume alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. However, multi-threaded performance is more constrained; stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registers in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 421.3 GB/sec, but the PassMark memory score and database operations fall into the weak tier.

Given its shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity, this server represents a budget-friendly option with high resource density, making it cost-efficient for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core utilization. The primary tradeoff is the performance drop under multi-threaded or memory-intensive operations, as evidenced by the weak database and multi-threaded decompression benchmarks. This configuration is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, and development or testing environments.
